justification: Fixes the two remaining findings from Sol's cross-review of PR #725, both provenance defects in the capacity engine's battleaxe handling. (a) _estimate_lot_dimensions guarded the head measurements by truthiness while the label guarded them by is-not-None, so a 0 measurement made the engine estimate from the WHOLE lot yet still tell the user the envelope was computed on the developable main lot - a silent wrong provenance claim on a liability-sensitive number. (b) the head depth is derived (area / width, i.e. head assumed rectangular) but was labelled as computed/measured, overclaiming precision. Regulatory-adjacent user-facing text plus capacity arithmetic, hence standard tier; the change is narrow and pinned by regression tests.

pre_impl.existing_data: Two independent guards on the same LotDimensions fields: _estimate_lot_dimensions used truthiness (0 -> falls back to the 1:2.5 whole-lot estimate) and compute_constraint_arithmetic's is_battleaxe_measured used is-not-None (0 -> True). They diverge at exactly 0/negative. No DB or query change - LotDimensions is in-memory, populated upstream.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: LotDimensions declares the battleaxe fields Optional[float], so pydantic coerces incoming numerics (e.g. a Decimal from a NUMERIC column) to float at the model boundary - verified live: LotDimensions(battleaxe_main_lot_width_m=Decimal('43.1')) yields a float and the predicate returns True. Only model_construct() would bypass that, and nothing in services/ uses it. Non-finite floats (inf) WOULD pass a naive >0 check and yield a 0 depth, so finiteness is checked.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new capability - a correctness/labelling fix. Single _has_battleaxe_head() predicate now shared by both call sites so they cannot drift apart again.

functions.name: _has_battleaxe_head
functions.input: the optional LotDimensions carrying lot_type and the head measurements
functions.output: True only for a battleaxe lot whose head width AND head area are finite positive numbers
functions.if_none: None / 0 / negative / non-finite / non-battleaxe all return False, so the caller estimates from the whole lot AND labels it as such - the two can no longer disagree

functions.name: _is_positive_measure
functions.input: a single candidate measurement value of unknown type
functions.output: True iff it is a finite, strictly positive, non-bool number
functions.if_none: None, bools, NaN, +/-inf, 0 and negatives all return False rather than being treated as a usable measurement

functions.name: _estimate_lot_dimensions
functions.input: the optional LotDimensions and the lot area in square metres
functions.output: a (frontage_m, depth_m) pair; for a battleaxe head it is (head width, head area / head width)
functions.if_none: without a usable head it falls through to frontage/depth, then the 1:2.5 area estimate; the head depth it returns is DERIVED, not measured, and the caller's gap note now says so

values.read_at: _has_battleaxe_head, then _estimate_lot_dimensions as the divisor for head depth
values.if_missing: treated as no usable head -> whole-lot 1:2.5 estimate AND the estimated-from-area gap note; a 0/inf width can no longer reach the division
treated as no usable head -> whole-lot fallback with the matching note, never a head-based provenance claim

break_it.scenario: A battleaxe lot arrives with battleaxe_main_lot_width_m = 0 and a valid head area
break_it.what_happens: Previously: _estimate_lot_dimensions fell back to the whole-lot 1:2.5 estimate, but is_battleaxe_measured stayed True, so the user was told 'envelope computed on the developable main lot, excluding the access handle' about a whole-lot guess - silent wrong provenance
break_it.how: both call sites now use the same _has_battleaxe_head predicate, which requires finite positive width AND area; a 0 means no head in both, so the output carries the 1:2.5 estimated-from-area note instead
break_it.repro: tests::TestBattleaxeDimensions::test_zero_width_head_does_not_claim_measured_envelope - asserts no 'main lot' note and that the 1:2.5 note is present

break_it.scenario: An irregular battleaxe head is described only by area and width, so depth is derived as area / width
break_it.what_happens: The old note said the envelope was 'computed on the developable main lot', implying a surveyed head; a non-rectangular head's real depth differs, so the figure was presented with more precision than it has
break_it.how: the note now states the envelope is 'estimated' from head area / width with the head 'assumed rectangular' and asks the reader to verify against the head's actual dimensions; the arithmetic is unchanged (and stays conservative: head area < lot area)
break_it.repro: tests::TestBattleaxeDimensions::test_head_envelope_note_is_an_estimate_not_a_measurement - asserts 'estimated' and 'assumed rectangular' present and the old 'computed on' wording gone

break_it.scenario: A head measurement is non-finite (inf) or a bool, or a Decimal arrives from a NUMERIC column
break_it.what_happens: An inf width passes a naive >0 check and makes area/width a 0 depth (0 footprint); a Decimal could be rejected by a strict float check and silently fall back to the whole lot
break_it.how: _is_positive_measure requires math.isfinite and excludes bools, so inf/NaN mean no head (whole-lot fallback WITH the matching note, not a false head claim). Decimal is a non-issue on every real path: the Optional[float] fields make pydantic coerce it to float at the model boundary - verified live - and nothing uses model_construct to bypass that; the docstring records this so the assumption is revisited if that changes
break_it.repro: tests::TestBattleaxeDimensions::test_head_predicate_agrees_with_estimation covers 0/negative/inf/NaN pairs; a live check confirmed LotDimensions(battleaxe_main_lot_width_m=Decimal('43.1')) -> float -> predicate True

post_merge.manual_verify: python -m pytest tests/test_constraint_arithmetic.py tests/test_capacity_golden.py tests/test_capacity_range.py tests/test_constraint_phased_ledger.py tests/test_dwelling_form.py -> 160 passed. Ran scripts/cross_review.py (gpt-5.6-sol) on this diff: its single HIGH finding (Decimal rejected by the float check) was VERIFIED AS A FALSE POSITIVE - pydantic coerces Decimal to float on every validated path and no code uses model_construct - but its 'finite floats' kernel was adopted as the math.isfinite guard. Both fixed findings originate from Sol's review of PR #725 and were hand-verified against the source before this fix.
